title: Peking-Style Roast Duck
subtitle: Crispy-skinned roast duck with pancakes and hoisin
excerpt: A home-cook's version of the great Chinese roast duck: duck legs lacquered with maltose and five-spice, roasted until the skin is paper-thin and shatteringly crisp, then served in steamed pancakes with hoisin sauce, cucumber, and spring onion.

recipe.sourceNotes: Peking duck (Beijing roast duck) is one of the most celebrated dishes in Chinese cuisine, with a history stretching back to the imperial era. Traditional Peking duck requires a whole duck that is inflated with air to separate the skin from the fat, blanched, coated in maltose, and air-dried for 24 hours before roasting in a specialist wood-fired oven; the process is a multi-day undertaking requiring professional equipment. This home version uses duck legs (which have the right fat-to-skin ratio) and achieves the crispy skin through a resting and air-drying period in the refrigerator, followed by roasting at high heat. The essential accompaniments are Mandarin pancakes (thin steamed pancakes available frozen from Chinese supermarkets), hoisin sauce, sliced cucumber, and spring onion.

content.text: Leave the duck legs uncovered in the fridge for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight; this dries the skin and is essential for achieving the crisp result. The skin must be completely dry before roasting. Score the skin in a crosshatch pattern (avoiding the meat) to help the fat render. Mandarin pancakes are sold frozen at Chinese supermarkets; steam them directly from frozen.

content.text: Mix the five-spice, soy, honey, vinegar, garlic, and ginger into a glaze. Season the duck legs with salt. Brush generously with the glaze. Leave uncovered in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.

Heat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Place the duck legs skin-side up on a rack over a roasting tin. Roast for 1 hour 30 minutes until the skin is deep mahogany and very crisp. Brush with extra glaze halfway through.

Rest the duck for 10 minutes. Shred the meat from the bone in large pieces. Serve on a large platter with steamed Mandarin pancakes, hoisin sauce, cucumber strips, and spring onion. Diners assemble their own wraps.
